- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to capture sharp upward moves; increase early forecast values, especially if sentiment turns bullish.
- Overshoots after spikes (e.g., 5.66→6.73, 10.55→12.98) are common; apply downward correction on day 2–5 post-spike.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts where model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; dampen extreme deviations from 18-day moving average.
- Horizon-specific error: 30d forecasts often overestimate later days (e.g., day 20–30) when sentiment is neutral or negative — reduce forecast tail (last 5–7 days) by 15–30% if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment history shows a recent spike followed by cooling, model tends to overcorrect — adjust forecast downward by 10–20% on day 1–3 after sentiment drop.
